## What each scenario is

- **Static page** — GET / — an 11.6 KB prerendered page, 200 + ETag
- **Revalidation (304)** — GET / with If-None-Match = that ETag
- **SSR, data unchanged** — GET /todos/t3 — rendered from path params + loaded data
- **SSR, data changes every request** — GET /live — nothing may be answered from memory

## Versions

- shinkansen (this commit) — this repo
- node:http v26.7.0 — raw Node, no framework
- Fastify 5.12.5
- Hono 4.13.8
- Express 5.2.1
- Next.js 16.3.6
- Nuxt 4.5.2

## Reading it honestly

- shinkansen answers a URL it has already answered from a table of pre-encoded bytes, because its ETag is the CID of those bytes. That is why it is lowest on the static page and the 304, and within noise on SSR while the data is unchanged.
- When the data changes on every request it is roughly 10× the plain Node servers: the app's render and the CID encoding run interpreted (kbb/sci) while the others run V8-JIT'd JavaScript. It is still below Next.js there.
- Next.js and Nuxt serve the same bytes through Route Handlers / Nitro server routes, with their best documented static option. Next.js's force-static route ignores If-None-Match, so its 304 is measured on a dynamic handler.
- The machine was shared (load average 60–180 during these runs). CPU per response holds up under that; requests per second does not.

Method, fixtures and how to re-run: [bench/README.md](https://github.com/kotoba-lang/shinkansen/blob/main/bench/README.md). Raw medians: [bench/results/2026-09-23-meta.edn](https://github.com/kotoba-lang/shinkansen/blob/main/bench/results/2026-09-23-meta.edn).
